audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer puts Volibear's stun on E and names it 'Hand of the God', then describes an 'empowered-Q dash' as a separate follow-up, and calls his R a shield-and-heal. All four are wrong.
audit.why: Riot's data: Thundering Smash (Q) is the ability that grants speed toward enemies and stuns the first one he attacks — the stun and the run-down are one 12s-at-rank-1 button. Sky Splitter (E) is a 1200-range lightning bolt that slows and shields him if he stands in it. Stormbringer (R) is a leap that grants bonus health and disables towers — no shield, no heal. 'Hand of the God' is not an ability in this kit.
audit.corrected: Every reference rebuilt on the real names and slots: Thundering Smash (Q) stun, Sky Splitter (E) slow-and-shield, Stormbringer (R) bonus health and tower disable.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart marks Levels 2 through First item as 'Skill' and then hands Lucian the 2+ items row, which is backwards from every prose line and from the packet chart.
audit.why: Volibear has no ranged tool and one 12s stun to Lucian's 500-range Q and dash-weave, so Lucian owns levels 2 through first item outright; late, Volibear's stacked HP and Frenzied Maul heal take the lane back.
audit.corrected: Rows 2-6 flipped to Lucian and the 2+ items row flipped to Volibear, in both layers, with ratings to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 line credits Lucian's ult without noting that Volibear's own ult is a 160s cooldown at rank 1 — the longest cooldown in the matchup and the reason the level-6 window belongs to Lucian.
audit.why: Stormbringer at 160/135/110 is far less available than The Culling at 110/100/90, so the 6-to-first-item stretch is Lucian's, not neutral.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states Stormbringer's 160s rank-1 cooldown as the punish window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is a trailing clause in the itemization line only; nothing states that Frenzied Maul is a 5s-cooldown heal, and nothing warns that it applies on-hit effects.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul's second cast on a marked target heals him on a flat 5s cooldown and applies on-hit item effects, so his damage scales with attack speed — armour alone misreads the trade and Grievous Wounds timing decides extended exchanges.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2] repurposed to the anti-heal buy against Frenzied Maul.

edits.before: Volibear is a slow, dash-once melee with no ranged poke, so Levels 1-3 are yours to bully. At 2 your Q plus the Lightslinger double-shot lands a heavy trade before his W bite is even worth casting, and your auto range alone keeps you out of his reach. The one thing to respect is his E stun — Hand of the God comes down from range, so don't tunnel an extended trade standing still where he can land it and follow with his empowered-Q dash. Throw Q, double-tap, and dash out before the bite slow sticks.
edits.after: Volibear is a slow melee with no ranged poke, so Levels 1-3 are yours to bully. At 2 your Q plus the Lightslinger double-shot lands a heavy trade before his W bite is even worth casting, and your auto range alone keeps you out of his reach. The button to respect is Thundering Smash (Q): he gains speed toward you and stuns the first thing he attacks, on a 12s cooldown at rank 1, so never stand still in an extended trade. Throw Q, double-tap, and dash out before Sky Splitter's slow lands.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 you stay firmly ahead but Voli starts stacking HP and his W bite heal claws back your poke, so trade in bursts rather than sitting in his face. Bait his E stun — once it's on cooldown he can't lock you for his dash, and that's your window to W-mark him, burst with a double-shot, and E away. At 6 your Culling executes a low Voli who has used E, but if he R's first to shield and heal, disengage and re-poke instead of channeling into his recovery.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 you stay firmly ahead but Voli starts stacking HP and Frenzied Maul's second bite claws your poke back every 5s, so trade in bursts rather than sitting in his face. Bait Thundering Smash — with that 12s stun down he cannot catch you at all, and that's your window to W-mark him, burst with a double-shot, and E away. At 6 your Culling executes a low Voli, but if he leaps in with Stormbringer for the bonus health, disengage and re-poke instead.

edits.before: This is where Volibear reclaims the lane — he's a tanky scaler and you're a weak-scaling ADC top. By two items his HP and W heal shrug off your poke, and one E stun plus an empowered-Q dash is enough to delete your low base HP. Your whole game plan is to convert the Levels 2-6 dominance into plates, kills, and a lead big enough that his scaling never catches up. If it goes even into the 2+ item window, play for sidelane safety and let your team answer the fed bear.

notes: This matchup carried the worst fabrication in my slice: the content layer invented 'Hand of the God' as an E stun and an 'empowered-Q dash' as a separate ability, and described Stormbringer as a shield-and-heal. Volibear's stun and his run-down are one ability, Thundering Smash (Q). All of it is corrected here. Whether Thundering Smash's stun can be cleansed or reduced by tenacity is not in the kit data and I asserted nothing about it.
